title: Analytics backfill Correction Runner: safe, idempotent reprocessing framework
creator: Aisha Mehta
description:
Problem statement:

We regularly need to reprocess historical telemetry and usage events for Console dashboards, billing pipelines, and feature analytics when bugs, missing fields, or schema evolution cause incorrect metrics. Current ad-hoc replays are slow, error-prone, and risk over-writing production conclusions. We need a first-class, auditable, tenant-scoped reprocessing framework that prioritizes safety, idempotency, and predictable cost.

Proposal summary:

Build an "Correction Runner" — a lightweight orchestration + worker framework for backfills and reprocessing runs. Key capabilities: idempotent transforms, dry-run/explain mode, tenant-scoped manifests, checkpointed windowed execution, adaptive rate/throttle to protect live ingestion SLO, cost estimation and safety budgets, end-to-end audit logs and lineage, and integration with Console UI for progress and approvals.

Why this is different from existing replay tools:
- Focus on safe corrections (patching / transforms) rather than raw replay of event streams.
- Built-in schema compatibility registry and transform validators to avoid silent data corruption.
- Explicit budget/safety gates and dry-run semantics before any writeback to downstream stores.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: Console analytics pipelines (event ingestion -> materialized metrics/billing/usage dashboards) and any data sinks we own (redshift/bigquery, clickhouse, search indices).
- Non-goal: Replacing low-level historical ingest orchestrator for full replays of raw encrypted payloads (those remain handled by infra replayer tools). Correction Runner focuses on derived-corrective transforms and targeted corrections for analytics/console use-cases.
acceptance_criteria: A run can be executed in dry-run mode and produce a validation report without mutating downstream sinks
A run can apply idempotent transform functions over a 30-day window for a tenant with 10M events and complete within estimated runtime
All writes performed by the runner are checkpointed and auditable; audit records contain transform sha, input hash, and output hash
Adaptive throttling prevents the reprocessor from increasing observed 95th percentile ingestion latency by >10% on primary pipelines (measured in canary tests)
Console displays run progress, estimated cost, and a fail-safe approval flow to allow a single-click rollback
Transforms are validated against a schema compatibility registry before being allowed to run in normal mode
design_decisions: Controller + worker model: central controller composes work windows and maintains checkpoints; workers execute transforms and report telemetry
Windowing: split historical time range into fixed-size windows with low-watermark checkpoints to allow partial resume and retries
Idempotency contract: every transform must accept (input_event, input_version) and produce deterministic output; system enforces event hashing and dedupe keys
Dry-run first: default runs start in dry-run/explain mode that produces diffs and metric projections; mutation requires explicit approval
Safety budget: operator-level budget config (max writes, max tokens, cost cap) and automatic pause when budget is consumed
Schema registry integration: before a run, the runner validates transforms against the target schema and enforces forward/backward compatibility rules
Adaptive throttle: a feedback loop samples live ingestion metrics and reduces concurrency when upstream SLOs degrade
implementation_plan: Week 0: Spec review and security signoff for writeback patterns; define transform interface and idempotency guidelines
Week 1-2: Implement controller API, job manifest format, and windowing logic; build basic dry-run path that reads events and runs transforms locally
Week 3-4: Worker pool implementation (k8s jobs), checkpointing with durable leases in coordination store (dynamo/etcd), and idempotent writer adapters for ClickHouse/BigQuery
Week 5: Safety features: budget enforcement, dry-run report generation, and schema compatibility checks
Week 6: Console UI integration for run creation, approval flow, progress, and cost estimation display
Week 7: Canary with non-critical tenant dataset, verify adaptive throttle behavior and rollback path
Week 8: Production rollout for analytics-only corrections and runbook publication
run_manifest_spec: target_sink: string (identifier of downstream target e.g., clickhouse-usage-v2)
transform_ref: string (hash or package name pointing at stored transform)
operational_runbook: How to preview: create a manifest with mode=dry-run; review generated Report S3 path in Console run detail
Approval flow: authorized users (analytics-admin, platform-ops) must switch mode to mutate via Console before writes can occur
Escalation: if the run observes >10% upstream latency spike, it will auto-pause and send alerts to #platform-reprocessing and oncall
Rollback: all mutations are written with a reversible marker and a snapshot of pre-run state where feasible; by default we perform logical reversions up to the last checkpoint
Post-mortem checklist: collect run report, sample pre/post diffs, check audit hashes, and confirm metrics are within tolerance
test_plan: Unit tests for transform harness with randomized property-based inputs
Integration test: run a dry-run against a 100k-event synthetic tenant dataset and verify hashes and diffs
Load test: simulate a 10M event backfill in staging with the adaptive throttle enabled and assert upstream latency stays within thresholds
Failure injection: kill worker mid-window and verify resume semantics using stored checkpoint

2025-02-20 - Marco Liu (Infra): We should avoid a global lock; use tenant-scoped leases and ensure cross-region tenants are split by region to keep latency predictable.
2025-02-28 - Security: Confirmed that writeback adapters will use customer-level KMS keys for sinks; we need a short security addendum before alpha.
2025-03-03 - Daniel Park: Updated plan to include adaptive throttle and added canary run step. Assigned implementation owner and estimate 8 pts.
notes: We intentionally keep the Correction Runner lightweight so teams can prototype transforms in-place without depending on infra replayers.
Transforms should be uploaded to an artifact registry with immutable hashes and an allowlist for production runs.
Require a short run preview window (first N minutes) as an automatic safety step before continuing larger windows
